newsitem.title: UK: Texaco sees Captain customers in NWE, N.America.
newsitem.headline: Texaco sees Captain customers in NWE, N.America.

text.p: Texaco Inc has outlets in Europe, the United States and Canada for crude oil from its North Sea Captain field due on stream shortly, a company representative in London said.
"We have homes in all of those locations," the representative said.
He said Texaco's Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam and its Pembroke refinery in Britain would be among installations receiving the crude.
Sales would be made on a variety of arrangements, including term, quarterly and spot contracts.
Refineries suitable for the grade would include speciality refineries making naphthenic lubes and high conversion plants.

He said Captain, a 21 degree API crude that has 0.7 percent sulphur content, had found homes in North America because refineries there had the flexibility to refine a broad range of crudes, including high sulphur and low gravity grades such as those from Venezuela and Saudi Arabia.
A Texaco spokeswoman said on Tuesday first oil from Captain had been postponed for a third time but the company hoped it would start "any time now".

Production at the 350-million barrel field was originally expected to begin late last year but an accident at the Spanish shipyard where the floating production and storage vessel (FPSO) was being built forced postponement to late January.
Captain is expected to reach peak production of some 60,000 barrels per day later this year.

The representative said Texaco was continuing to assess whether to implement a second development phase that would raise production to around 100,000 bpd. Experts have said the field could have a life of 20 years.
